test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 4 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Who among the following can propose a Government Bill?

options.text: Member of the Treasury Bench in Lok Sabha
A Member of Parliament who is not a Minister
Minister in either House of Parliament

solution:
The correct answer is __**Minister in either House of Parliament**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Minister in either House of Parliament can propose **a Government Bill.
 
• **A bill introduced by a Minister is called a Government Bill, **while **a bill introduced by a Member of Parliament who is not a Minister is called a Private Member's Bill.**
 
• **A bill is a draft statute that becomes law after it is passed by both Houses of Parliament and approved by the President.**
 
• A bill that is related to **taxation, borrowing, expenditure, audits, and accounting is called a Money Bill.**
 
• Only **a Minister can introduce a Money Bill in Parliament, and it must be recommended by the President first.**
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final say on whether a bill is a Money Bill. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Bill-There are four types of bills in our Constitution. 

 
 
• Ordinary bill-Ordinary bill is a bill that can be introduced in either by houses of any minister or member of the both houses.
 
• Money bill-Money Bill refers to a bill that is introduced in the Lower Chamber of Indian Parliament(Lok Sabha) which generally covers the issue of spending and receipt of money, such as law-related with, laws of any governing borrowing, and also government expenditure.
 
• Finance bill-Finance Bill is a secret bill introduced each year in Lok Sabha(Lower chamber of the Parliament) immediately after the implementation of the Union Budget, to enact some effect to the financial proposals of the Government of India. 
 
• Constitutional amendment bills-Bills seeking to amend all other provisions of the Constitution including those enumerated in the provision to article 368(2), are called by the title 'Constitution Amendment Bills'.These Bills can be introduced in the House of Parliament.
